prompt: Implement service_identity(reference, certificate) returning a Boolean. reference is {'kind':'DNS'|'IP','value':string}; certificate is {'dns_sans':[strings],'ip_sans':[valid_IP_strings],'common_name':string_or_None}. This component performs only RFC-9525 DNS-ID/IP-ID matching, not certificate-path validation, expiry, private-key proof or application authorization. DNS reference values are normalized valid ASCII LDH hostnames with no trailing dot or empty label; Unicode, IDNA/A-label ('xn--') processing, ports, zone IDs, SRV-ID and URI-ID are excluded. DNS SANs are normalized ASCII names or wildcard patterns; '*' alone is excluded from inputs, and other patterns have at least one fixed label. Ignore unsupported wildcard placements. Exact DNS matching compares labels case-insensitively. Support a wildcard only when the sole '*' occupies the complete leftmost label, and match exactly one nonempty reference label with all remaining label counts and contents equal. Do not add a public-suffix or minimum-domain-depth policy; '*.test' can match 'api.test' in this identity-only component, independently of issuance/trust rules. IP references are valid bare IPv4/IPv6 strings and match only iPAddress SANs by same-family address octets, accepting equivalent IPv6 textual forms. Never use IP-looking dNSName text or Common Name as an IP-ID, never fall back to CN for any reference, and never infer the reference kind from a presented SAN. Return True if any identifier of the required type matches, otherwise False. Inputs must remain unchanged and calls are independent.

Implement ech_recovery(ech_accepted, negotiated_tls13, handshake_ok, identity_ok, retry_configs='absent', allow_non_ech_retry=False). This is a terminal recovery-decision component for a real ECH offer under RFC 9849 Section 6.1.6, not a TLS implementation. All flags are actual booleans. handshake_ok supplies base protocol/Finished validation; identity_ok supplies private-origin identity validation for accepted ECH, or ECHConfig.public_name validation for rejected ECH. retry_configs is 'absent', 'unsupported', 'supported', or 'malformed'; unsupported means a syntactically valid list with no client-supported ECH VERSION, while supported means a supported version and usable parameters. Supported-version-but-unusable-parameter cases are out of scope. Inputs use valid combinations: accepted ECH uses TLS 1.3 and absent retry_configs; negotiated_tls13=False means locally permitted TLS 1.2, rejected ECH and absent retry_configs. Return exactly {'original_success':bool,'send_application':bool,'action':str}. Any failed handshake or identity check returns False/False/'fail'. Accepted ECH with both checks passed returns True/True/'complete'. Every rejected offer returns False/False regardless of outer authentication. After successful rejected-outer authentication, malformed retry configurations fail; usable supported configurations select 'retry-ech'; absent/unsupported configurations or the permitted older-version branch select 'retry-without-ech' only when allow_non_ech_retry is True, otherwise 'fail'. This selected strategy follows the recommended supported-configuration retry. send_application concerns permission at this gate on the original connection, not whether earlier 0-RTT existed. Every retry action means a fresh transport connection after terminating the rejected outer; it grants no separate DIRECT-origin fallback permission or bypass of SVCB endpoint/client policy. Each call is independent.

Implement hsts_trace(events) for a bounded dynamic HSTS policy ledger and request-processing component. Return one snapshot per event with exactly known_hsts (bool), scheme (None|'http'|'https'), port (None|int), must_terminate (None|bool), and policies (map from lowercase host to {'expires_at':int,'include_subdomains':bool}). Events have nondecreasing nonnegative integer time and host. Hosts are normalized ASCII DNS names without trailing dots, Unicode, IDNA or legacy numeric-IP syntax, or canonical bare IPv4/IPv6 addresses without brackets/zone IDs. Header events are {'type':'header','time':t,'host':h,'secure':bool,'transport_ok':bool,'max_age':nonnegative_int,'include_subdomains':bool}; the caller has already parsed valid STS syntax. Request events are {'type':'request','time':t,'host':h,'scheme':'http'|'https','port':None_or_1_to_65535,'transport_error':bool}, with transport_error describing the attempted transport after any required upgrade. Before each event discard entries with expires_at<=time. Learn/update only error-free secure-transport headers for DNS hosts; ignore IP-literal, insecure and failed-transport headers. Positive max_age sets only that host's expiry to time+max_age and its includeSubDomains flag. Zero removes only that exact host entry, preserving ancestor and descendant entries. Known HSTS applies to an active exact entry or an active ancestor with includeSubDomains, using DNS-label boundaries and case-insensitive host comparison; IP literals never match. Upgrade a known host's HTTP request to HTTPS, changing explicit port 80 to 443, preserving every other explicit port, and preserving None as an implicit port (the new HTTPS default is 443). Already-HTTPS requests retain their explicit port. For requests, must_terminate is True exactly when HSTS applies and transport_error is True; False only means this HSTS rule does not require termination and is not permission to ignore other TLS checks. For header observations scheme/port/must_terminate are None, with no connection-attempt decision. known_hsts reports policy applicability after the event for its host. Start each call empty; use no preload/HTTPS-only rules, real network, retained call state, or input mutation. Historical snapshot values must remain stable during later processing.

Implement traffic_updates(secret_hex, generations) returning a list of lowercase hexadecimal strings. secret_hex is exactly 64 hex digits, in either case, representing a 32-byte SYNTHETIC current SHA256 TLS 1.3 application traffic secret; generations is an integer from 0 through 4. Return new secrets secret_1 through secret_generations, excluding the initial input; zero generations returns []. Each step applies RFC 9846 Section 7.2 HKDF-Expand-Label(current,'traffic upd',empty_context,32), using RFC 5869 HKDF-Expand without an additional Extract operation. Encode HkdfLabel as big-endian uint16 output length 32, then uint8 byte length of ASCII 'tls13 traffic upd', those label bytes, uint8 context length 0, and no context bytes. There is no NUL terminator or substituted transcript hash. Feed each derived 32-byte secret into the next update generation and emit exactly 64 lowercase hex digits per result. Use standard-library hashlib/hmac only; no network, real session keys, random entropy, AEAD records or full TLS handshake/state machine is modeled. Each call is independent.

Implement firewall_return_gate(packet, states, now, return_rule=True, deny_rule=False), returning exactly {'admit':bool,'reason':str}. This is a chosen state-only return-packet policy over supplied previously validated outbound flow records, not a TCP parser, TLS identity verifier, or payload-safety oracle. Each state has instance (nonempty string), protocol ('tcp'|'udp'), src and dst (two-element [canonical_IPv4_string,integer_port_1_to_65535] lists), and expires_at (nonnegative integer clock tick). packet has instance/protocol/src/dst plus ack (raw untrusted bool, False for UDP) and transition_ok (bool supplied by an independent protocol-transition validator). now is an abstract nonnegative integer tick. A live reverse match needs the same instance and protocol, both IP-and-port endpoints exactly reversed, and now<expires_at. Multiple stale/current records may describe a tuple; any one live exact reverse match suffices. Apply precedence: deny_rule=True returns False/'deny-rule'; return_rule=False returns False/'return-rule-disabled'; no live reverse match returns False/'no-live-reverse-state'; failed transition_ok returns False/'bad-transition'; otherwise return True/'state'. The ACK bit never creates permission. All flag inputs are actual booleans. No independent new-flow/stateless allowance, state creation, refresh or retained cross-call permission is modeled, and input objects must not be mutated.
